// Build the model prompt as plain text. Curly braces are stripped because the
// agent node runs the prompt through a template where { } mean variables.
const b = $('Webhook').first().json.body
const clean = (v) => String(v ?? '').replace(/[{}]/g, '')
const lines = [
  'Today: ' + clean(b.today),
  'Default account id: ' + clean(b.defaultAccountId),
  'Accounts (id | name):',
  ...(b.accounts || []).map(a => '  ' + clean(a.id) + ' | ' + clean(a.name)),
  'Categories (id | name):',
  ...(b.categories || []).map(c => '  ' + clean(c.id) + ' | ' + clean(c.name)),
  'Text: ' + clean(b.text),
]
return [{ json: { prompt: lines.join('\n') } }]

options.systemMessage: You turn one line of casual text about money into a single JSON transaction for a personal ledger. Reply with ONLY a JSON object, no prose, no code fences, with keys: accountId (string, one of the provided account ids), categoryId (string, one of the provided category ids), amount (number; NEGATIVE for spending, positive only when money was clearly received), note (short clean label like "McDonald's" or "Grab to work", never the whole sentence), occurredAt (YYYY-MM-DD; use today unless the text names a date like 'yesterday' or 'sept 3'), confidence ("high" or "low"; low when the category is a guess or the amount is unclear), explanation (one short sentence saying which category/account you picked and why). Choose the best-fitting category from the list; if nothing fits use the one named 'Running Budget'. Use the default account unless the text names another account (e.g. 'on BPI', 'gcash'). Amounts are Philippine pesos; strip currency words and commas. If there is genuinely no amount, return a JSON object whose only key is error with the value no amount found.
